newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht rallies to highest since 1984 offshore.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht rallies to highest since 1984 offshore.

text.p: The Thai baht rallied to its highest level since 1984 against the dollar in the offshore market early on Thursday as foreign players scrambled for baht, dealers said.

The baht jumped to 23.900/24.000 to the dollar early offshore from 24.360/24.410 late on Wednesday. The baht/dollar spot rate offshore was at its highest level since Thailand's last baht devaluation in 1984.
In the local market, the baht was quoted much softer at 25.835/25.840, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand on Thursday fixed the mid-rate at 25.82 per dollar, unchanged from Wednesday.

A two-tier offshore and onshore baht market has been in place since mid-May after speculative attacks on the currency prompted the central bank to impose what dealers called capital controls to cut off baht supplies to offshore speculators.
As the offshore scramble for baht raged, The Bank of Thailand on Thursday denied market talk that it would buy dollars in the offshore markets at 24.00 baht.

A senior central bank official told Reuters that the talk was that the Bank of Thailand would make the move to help bail out speculators caught with short baht positions and were now hit by capital controls imposed by the central bank.
"We have no interest whatsoever to buy dollars in the offshore market," the official told Reuters.
Dealers said the central bank's denial was aimed at hitting back at speculators who held positions against the baht.
"We heard the talk in offshore market. But nobody here believed it as we know the central bank wants to strike back at those speculators," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was quoted at 130/170 satangs per dollar in offshore and 20/30 in domestic market.
The overnight interbank rate was steady 15.00-15.50 in early morning compared with 15.00-16.00 late on Wednesday.
Dealers said interbank rates would stay high for the rest of this week due to strong demand for funds for mid-year corporate tax payment and central bank reserve requirement.
